        ### Question
        A 52-year-old Caucasian male presents to your office with an 8 mm dark lesion on his back. The lesion, as seen below, has irregular borders and marked internal color variation. Upon excisional biopsy, the presence of which of the following would best estimate the risk of metastasis in this patient’s lesion:?

        ### Options
        opa. Palisading nuclei
opb. Keratin pearls
opc. Vertical tumor growth
opd. Cellular atypia
ope. Increased production of melanosomes

### Reasoning Chains per Option:
CHAIN: "Irregular borders and marked internal color variation" -> "suspicion of melanoma" -> "excisional biopsy performed" -> "histopathological examination" -> "identification of cellular atypia" -> "increased risk of metastasis" -> 80% CHAIN: "Excisional biopsy" -> "identification of vertical tumor growth" -> "increased risk of metastasis" -> 75% CHAIN: "Presence of palisading nuclei" -> "suggestive of basal cell carcinoma" -> "lower risk of metastasis" -> 70% CHAIN: "Increased production of melanosomes" -> "suggestive of melanoma" -> "increased risk of metastasis" -> 80%

           - Remove/adjust steps contradicting known facts.
           - If paths confirm or clarify a point aligned with consensus, use them.
           - Ignore irrelevant or overly broad paths that don't help.
